title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets (abstract page)
note: Fetched. v1 submitted 5 Nov 2026 by Genov, Martinez Alonso and Bergmeir; cs.LG and eess.SY; CC BY 4.0. Headline: over 32 live days weather covariates cut the error of each of ten foundation models by 37 to 51% on matched races (64 to 73% wind, 48 to 61% solar); zero-shot they match or beat LightGBM on the same covariates; on load the gap to the operators is 4 to 6%, within intervals.

title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets (full text, v1)
note: Fetched. Design: every day at 11:30 CET, before the 12:00 day-ahead gate, each model forecasts the 96 quarter-hours of the next day for price, wind, solar and load in BE, NL, FR, DE-LU, DK1, DK2. The benchmark runs all models itself on one frozen, published input set; context is 28 days of 15-minute history. Live since 2 Oct 2026; load added 6 Oct.

title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets (full text, v1)
note: Weather inputs: ICON-EU, GFS and IFS HRES runs from the Open-Meteo single-runs archive, admitted only if published before the cut-off, sampled at 153 capacity-weighted points (load: population-weighted). Foundation models get three or four ensemble means and spreads per target; LightGBM and ridge get the whole table plus calendar. Load models do not get the operators' load forecast since 16 Oct.

title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets (full text, v1)
note: Coverage: issue days 2 Oct to 2 Nov 2026. Load has 28 scored days in BE and FR, 22 in NL, 19 in DE-LU; Danish load is left out (partial actuals). 22 of 24 series, 16 to 32 days each. Scores are MAE pooled per series relative to a same-quarter-hour-last-week naive, geometric mean over series; Elo from a Bradley-Terry fit with a 95% day-bootstrap interval.

title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets (full text, v1)
note: Table 6, same model without and with covariates on shared races: Chronos-2 0.569 to 0.295 (-48% all; price -34, wind -67, solar -57, load -4), 31 days, 525 races. TimesFM 3.0 -51% (load -1), Timestral -46% (load -3), t0-gamma -48% (load -13), TiRex-2 -45% (load +4), TimesFM 2.5 via ridge -37% (load +31). Text: on load the change is small because history already carries the cycles.

title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets (full text, v1)

title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets (full text, v1)
note: Against LightGBM: four of five native-covariate models beat lgbm_cov trained on the 28-day context (0.282 to 0.320 against 0.330 to 0.337), t0-alpha is level. LightGBM gets more of the table. On load lgbm_cov is worse than the naive (1.018 to 1.026) because 28 days are too few; lgbm_prod trained on two years reaches 0.293 overall, inside the foundation models' range.

title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets (full text, v1)
note: Table 7, against the operators' pre-gate forecast on 141 shared races (16 Oct to 2 Nov, eight series): Chronos-2 +20% overall (95% +6 to +35), load +8%; Timestral +11% (0 to +23), load +6%; t0-gamma +13%, load +4%; TimesFM 3.0 load +21%; lgbm_prod load +22%. On load the closest models are 1 to 11% better in BE, NL and DE-LU and 41 to 59% worse in FR.

title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets (full text, v1)
note: Limitations as the authors state them: one autumn month; standings provisional; entry configurations fixed before going live but chosen by authors who had seen earlier weeks; the analyses and comparison windows were not registered in advance; six days had an incomplete ICON-EU run; Dutch targets changed definition; load models received the operators' forecast as an input until 15 Oct.

title: ujohn33/foretec-energy-bench (repository)
note: Fetched. Apache-2.0 code, CC BY 4.0 data and scores; 300 commits; built on sktime. README states the cut-off and no-look-ahead rules, the same-vintage rule for training weather, how to add a model, and that Chronos-2, Chronos-Bolt, TimesFM 2.5 and 3, Moirai 2, TiRex, Toto, Sundial and TTM r2 run in their own environments. Forecasts, actuals and scores are published on the site and on Hugging Face.

title: research: primary sources for and against the claim
note: One standard-tier call, LinkedIn excluded, 8 sources. Its reading: the 37 to 51% gain is pooled over targets and comes from wind and solar; on load covariates change error by -13% to +4%; no single load winner is established; lgbm_cov has the same weather but only 28 days; forecasts are locked live but the analyses were not pre-registered; no independent replication or critique found.
